sweep_summary: Two works with stress in the title, both by V. A. Dybo on 'Tubu' = Lukas 1953's Kashirda (Keshirda) Daza, the same dialect as the catalog's source Walters 2015. (1) Dybo 1987 (100-pp chapter, Russian; Glottolog ref) was found open on inslav.ru, downloaded, scanned (image-only 2-up scan; 300 dpi for the key pages, 200 dpi elsewhere) and read: preliminary contour rule p. 469 'ударение ставится на первый высокий тон словоформы' (stress on the first high tone of the word-form; falling = high), conclusion p. 553 (an earlier reading distribution linked to tone schemes by a Balto-Slavic-type contour rule; tones fading; system intermediate between tone and paradigmatic accent). (2) Dybo 1994 (English, St. Petersburg Journal of African Studies, two parts 2: 29-50 and 3: 27-44 per Dybo's own bibliography) has no open copy anywhere located; but its Russian text, Dybo 1995 MLJ 1: 236-279 (same work per Dybo's bibliography item 105), was downloaded from inslav.ru and read in full: p. 269 final rule 'акцент.. падает.. на первый слог с высоким тоном', p. 240 verbs form barytone (H root) vs oxytone (L root) accent types, p. 239 quotes Lukas 1953: 7 verbatim on the 'starker Akzent (Druck)'. Both refine rather than contradict the catalog's tonal / pitch accent coding (Walters 2015): they supply a stress statement Walters lacks -- dynamic stress predictable as the first H-toned syllable, i.e. the left edge of Walters's obligatory contiguous H-span -- while keeping placement tone-driven and lexically distributed. Recommended: keep Walters 2015 as deciding source, add Dybo 1987: 469/553 and Dybo 1995: 240, 269 as supporting sources with the first-H stress rule; Lukas 1953: 7-8 (De Gruyter DOI 10.1515/9783112766194, paywalled) remains the primary data source worth acquiring. All files under ( and updated). discovery used direct downloads of inslav.ru, archive.org, Crossref and Semantic Scholar APIs.

new_statements.quote: Внутренняя реконструкция (анализ системы в терминах акцентуационных валентностей и сравнение результатов с тоновыми схемами III глагольной группы), подтверждаемая непосредственным сравнением с тонами канури, позволяет установить, что акцент в тубу регулируется контурным правилом балто-славянского типа, т.е. акцент падает на начало первой последовательности морфем (соответственно, слогов) высшей валентности, иначе говоря, на первый слог с высоким тоном (соответственно, с восходящим или нисходящим тоном, которые приравниваются в контурном правиле к высокому).
new_statements.translation: Internal reconstruction (analysis of the system in terms of accentual valencies and comparison of the results with the tone schemes of verb group III), confirmed by direct comparison with the tones of Kanuri, allows us to establish that accent in Tubu is governed by a contour rule of the Balto-Slavic type, i.e. the accent falls on the beginning of the first sequence of morphemes (correspondingly, syllables) of higher valency -- in other words, on the first syllable with high tone (or with rising or falling tone, which the contour rule treats as high).

new_statements.reading: Dybo, working from the stress-marked verb paradigms in Lukas 1953 (Kashirda/Keshirda Daza -- the same dialect Walters 2015 describes), finds that Tubu/Dazaga has a dynamic stress (Lukas's 'starker Akzent (Druck)') whose position is fully predictable from tone: it falls on the first high-toned syllable of the word-form, falling and rising tones counting as high. Verbs split into barytona (H root, root stress) and oxytona (L root, ending stress); tone classes of preformatives are lexical. He characterises the system as tone in a 'fading' state, transitional between a classical tone system and a paradigmatic-accent system (1987: 554). This is consistent with, and adds a stress rule to, Walters's pitch accent analysis (one obligatory contiguous H-span per word; Dybo's an earlier reading is the left edge of that span). It does not turn Dazaga into a positional or weight-sensitive stress language: placement is tone-conditioned and lexically distributed, so the catalog's tonal/pitch accent coding stands, with 'stress = first H syllable (Dybo 1987/1995, from Lukas 1953)' as a refinement.

tone_statements.quote: Ударение в тубу, по крайней мере, в глагольной системе образует два акцентных типа ... правило, которым регулируется постановка акцента в словоформе, теснейшим образом связано с тональной схемой этой словоформы. tone_statements.translation: Stress in Tubu, at least in the verbal system, forms two accent types ... the rule that governs the placement of the accent in the word form is most closely tied to the tonal scheme of that word form. Preliminarily the contour rule can be formulated as follows: the stress is placed on the first high tone of the word form, a falling tone counting as high for this rule. 1.2.1. The tonal schemes of word forms are composed of the tone of the root and the tonal schemes of the conjugation suffixes

audit.reasoning: Quote check: both the 'quote' and 'the domain quotation' passages and the fn. 28 exception are verbatim in the Walters 2015 PDF we hold at Section 3.4, printed pp. 34-35, as the locator says. Deciding source: a 2015 MA-thesis grammar by the author of the only modern reference grammar (Brill 2016), open text, with tonal minimal triplets and an explicit obligatoriness/culminativity argument; no mention of stress anywhere in the work. Every earlier description Walters cites (Lukas 1953, Amani 1986, Alidou 1988, Wolff & Alidou 1989, Wolff 1991) treats Dazaga as tonal, disagreeing only on the number of tonemes, so the 'tonal / no stress rule' coding is not at risk. WALS has no prosody values for Tubu. sources.quote: Die Tubusprache besitzt einen starken Akzent (Druck), der der Sprache einen energischen Charakter verleiht. In welcher Weise der Akzent rhythmisch im Satz verteilt wird, bedarf näherer Untersuchung. Der Ton spielt auch im Tubu eine nicht zu unterschätzende Rolle. ... eine große Anzahl von Verbalwurzeln ist hoch- bzw. tieftonig, wodurch die Tonfolgen der Verbalformen bestimmt werden und regelmäßige Tonschemata entstehen [Lukas 1953, S. 7].
sources.note: Foundational Tubu grammar; pp. 7-8 treat tone (cited by Walters). Would show whether the older literature ever described a word accent ('Akzent') rather than tone.
